name: Microsoft App Center analytics and crashes
plain: Microsoft's analytics and crash SDK, retired by Microsoft in 2025.
meaning: Sent device model, OS, app version and crash traces to Microsoft. Retirement means newer builds should have replaced it.

android.note: Seen in Exodus reports for 4.1.637 and 4.1.995; retired by Microsoft on 31 March 2025 (verify current build)

limits.headline: Can send usage and crash reports to Microsoft's retired tracking service from the Android app
limits.user_action: Nothing. It runs when the app starts or crashes
can: Send crash reports and usage counts over the internet
Run with no prompt after install
Appear in some LinkedIn Android builds (4.1.637 and 4.1.995 were checked)
cannot: Keep running as a Microsoft service; it was retired on 31 March 2025
Show up on iPhone; no evidence was found there
Prove it is active today; the finding comes from code scans, so check the current build
limits.reach_label: While the app runs, usage and crashes
limits.differs: Seen only in the Android app; no iPhone evidence was found.

story.what_it_is: A Microsoft toolkit that sent crash reports and usage counts from an app.

marketing.name: App Center retirement
marketing.pitch: Microsoft announced it would shut App Center down on March 31, 2025, and told developers to move to other tools.

story.for_you: You never saw it. It sent your phone model, system version and the app's crash details to Microsoft so engineers could fix bugs. It is retired, so newer builds should no longer use it.
story.for_makers: Gave small teams free crash reports, usage numbers and test builds. Makers watched it to catch bugs after a release, then moved to other tools when Microsoft closed it.

use_cases.example: A work app learns that version 9.2 crashes on one phone model after an update and rolls out a fix.
A small game studio finds the level that crashes older phones and patches it that weekend.
A team counts how many people used a new screen and which phones they used.
A company tests a new build with a small group before sending it to everyone.
A developer receives crash traces with the line of code and a device summary for each failure.

risks: Sends device details to a third party
story.android_note: Android builds could carry this code until the service ended.
story.ios_note: iOS builds could carry it too, but Apple's privacy labels required the app to say so.

linkedin.how: Exodus reports for LinkedIn 4.1.637 and 4.1.995 list App Center Analytics and Crashes. Microsoft owns LinkedIn, so sharing is intra-group.
